title: Microsoft Edge: sign in to Edge with a Google account on Windows and macOS
summary: Hold: both Group Policy routes start inside Administrative Templates rather than giving the navigation needed to reach it. The feature's availability, default permission and registry settings are supported, but the assurance that it takes no action on its own is not documented.

claims.claim: Google or Apple sign-in buttons appear in the profile flyout and unified sign-in experience when available and permitted.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Disabling NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled blocks non-Microsoft sign-in and hides and disables its entry points.
claims.quote: If you disable this policy, users can't sign in to Microsoft Edge with non-Microsoft accounts. Related sign-in entry points and code paths are hidden and disabled, regardless of related feature flag settings.

claims.quote: Users can still sign in with Microsoft accounts.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The policy covers non-Microsoft accounts such as Google and Apple, while the roadmap names Google.
claims.quote: This policy controls whether users can sign in to Microsoft Edge using non-Microsoft accounts, such as Google or Apple accounts.

claims.claim: The full Group Policy route begins Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Identity and sign-in > Enable sign-in to Microsoft Edge using non-Microsoft accounts.
claims.quote: To configure a mandatory policy, open the Group Policy Editor and go to (Computer Configuration or User Configuration) > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path with 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Identity and sign-in > Enable sign-in to Microsoft Edge using non-Microsoft accounts'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge for the navigation prefix; the existing policy reference supplies the remaining steps.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: table; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The registry setting is NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled, REG_DWORD, under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled; Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.claim: The full Group Policy route begins Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Restrict which accounts can be used to sign in to Microsoft Edge.
claims.quote: To configure a mandatory policy, open the Group Policy Editor and go to (Computer Configuration or User Configuration) > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path with 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Restrict which accounts can be used to sign in to Microsoft Edge'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge for the navigation prefix; the existing policy reference supplies the remaining steps.

claims.claim: The registry setting is RestrictSigninToPattern, REG_SZ, under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: RestrictSigninToPattern; Value type: REG\_SZ

claims.claim: RestrictSigninToPattern uses a regular-expression pattern.
claims.quote: You can configure this policy to match multiple accounts using a Perl style regular expression for the pattern.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: RestrictSigninToPattern limits browser sign-in to accounts whose usernames match its pattern.
claims.quote: If a user tries to sign in to the browser with an account whose username doesn't match this pattern, they're blocked and will get the appropriate error message.

claims.claim: Enabling RestrictSigninToPattern signs out already signed-in profiles whose usernames do not match.
claims.quote: Signed-in profiles with a username that doesn't match this pattern will be signed out after this policy is enabled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The RestrictSigninToPattern page does not explicitly name Google or Apple accounts, so its applicability should not be relied on alone.
claims.quote: Determines which accounts can be used to sign in to the Microsoft Edge account that's chosen during the Sync opt-in flow. ... If you don't configure this policy or leave it blank, users can use any account to sign in to Microsoft Edge.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].note's final sentence and the matching prose caveat with 'The policy determines which accounts can be used during the Sync opt-in flow.' The reference states this general reach without restricting it to Microsoft accounts: https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/restrictsignintopattern.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in licensing price meter Edge for Business license; Microsoft Edge for Business free licensing browser license cost. Read NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled, Edge for Business, and Stable release notes; none names a licence for this feature.

claims.claim: The roadmap, policy reference and Stable release notes name no meter or charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in licensing price meter Edge for Business license. Read the roadmap, NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled, Edge for Business and the Google sign-in passages in Stable 150 and 154 release notes; no feature meter or charge is named.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe which browser data a Google-signed-in Edge profile synchronises.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in sync data storage synchronization. Read the policy and release notes plus privacy Sync and enterprise-sync search excerpts; they describe Microsoft-account or enterprise sync, not Google-profile sync data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the service or storage destination for Google-profile sync.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in sync data storage synchronization. Read NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled, Stable release notes and privacy Sync excerpts; Microsoft-account sync uses Microsoft servers, but Google-profile sync is not described.

claims.claim: The feature takes no action on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign-in automatic actions autonomous NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled. Read the policy, Stable Google sign-in release notes and identity/privacy excerpts; none states the complete absence of automatic actions for Google sign-in.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the feature adds a sign-in option and takes no action on its own.' with 'The roadmap describes a Google account sign-in option in the profile menu and Edge sign-in screen.'
